login: migrate to generalized MOCK_METHOD() macro This CL replaces the uses of MOCK_METHOD*() and MOCK_CONST_METHOD*() macros in unit tests with the generalized MOCK_METHOD() macro, which is now the recommended way to define mocked methods with gmock. In particular, MOCK_METHOD() supports annotating a mocked method with specifiers such as 'override'. One minor change is that argument names are omitted in the argument list provided to MOCK_METHOD() in order to prevent clang-format from formatting code like `Foo* foo` into `Foo * foo`. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests. Change-Id: I76254842eefaec383afec157f4d294c08b4ee509 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1810098 Tested-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ben Chan <benchan@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org>

diagnostics: Add DPSL test utilities Command line utilities to test DPSL communication into and out of a VM. The requester utility sends an outgoing gRPC request to wilco_dtc_supportd and prints the returned response. The response is printed as JSON, so you can see both the name and the actual content of the proto. The listener utility blocks indefinitely, monitoring and printing any incoming gRPC requests from wilco_dtc_supportd. The request is printed as JSON, so you can see both the name and the actual content of the proto. BUG=b:138329362 TEST=First cherry pick https://crrev.com/c/1788380 to add utils to ebuild. Then: emerge-sludge diagnostics-dpsl-test && \ ./build_image --board=sludge base && \ termina_build_image \ --image ~/trunk/src/build/images/sludge/latest/*.bin \ --output ~/trunk/src/my/vms/sludge && \ scp -r ~/trunk/src/my/vms/sludge/* root@${DUT}:/opt/wilco/dtc-vm Then see the help messages in the two files for how to use. Change-Id: I3a0e0bbab4243418a388f3dfad7e42980ba110ce Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1767044 Tested-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Oleh Lamzin <lamzin@google.com>

FROMLIST: tracing: Fix possible double free on failure of allocating trace buffer commit 4397f04575c44e1440ec2e49b6302785c95fd2f8 upstream. Jing Xia and Chunyan Zhang reported that on failing to allocate part of the tracing buffer, memory is freed, but the pointers that point to them are not initialized back to NULL, and later paths may try to free the freed memory again. chaps: Use RSA_generate_key_ex() As of OpenSSL 0.9.8, RSA_generate_key() is deprecated in favor of RSA_generate_key_ex(). RSA_generate_key_ex() requires passing in a BIGNUM* exponent, for which we use a crypto::ScopedBIGNUM. Make these changes along with adding proper NULL->nullptr and NULL checks. The end result is no functional change, but better alignment for openssl 1.1 migration. arc: networkd: Apply BPF filter to NDProxy socket This change apply a BPF filter to the AF_PACKET socket created by NDProxy, so that instead of receiving all IPv6 packets and filter later in user space, all unrelated packets are filtered out in kernel and only ICMPv6 ND packets will be received. CHROMIUM: mm: checking min_filelist_kbytes in global reclaim There are 2 types of memory reclaim: 1. global reclaim is triggered when system free memory is under global memory watermark. 2. memcg reclaim is triggered when memory usage of a memcg exceeded its limit. Reserving file pages in global reclaim is sufficient to avoid system-wide file page thrashing. In file_is_low(), comparing min_filelist_kbytes against node file pages instead of lruvec file pages. Lruvec file pages contains only the file pages in a specific cgroup.
